cases.source_note: GAAP Q3 operating revenue including fuel surcharges.
cases.reason: Heartland’s October 14, 2021 release establishes that Q3 consolidated GAAP operating revenue was $152,612,000, including fuel surcharges. The comparable Q3 2020 figure was $162,282,000. The 95% cutoff was $154,167,900, which actual revenue undershot by $1,555,900. The earliest public date remains unresolved because I could verify the June 4 KeyBanc and June 8 UBS event notice but could not recover Heartland’s remarks, a complete presentation, or an official recording for either event. The upper bound below is the verified October actual. The results exhibit is headed “October 14, 2021 For Immediate Release,” and Heartland’s press-release archive independently dates the Q3 announcement October 14. This verifies public disclosure of actuals four days before the October 18 Form 8-K filing. The content of the two June sessions remains unverified.

cases.source_note: Quarterly operating revenue including fuel surcharges, with both companies in the groups as reported.
cases.reason: Heartland publicly established the decline by January 31, 2024. Consolidated GAAP operating revenue, including fuel surcharges, was $275,347,000 for October–December 2023 versus $354,923,000 for October–December 2022. That was a 22.42% decline, below the $337,176,850 cutoff. Both quarters included Smith Transport and CFI for all three months. The earliest date remains unresolved because the September 12 Morgan Stanley and November 7 Baird conference records recovered do not establish what Heartland management said. The upper bound below is the verified actual. Exhibit 99.1 is dated January 31, 2024 and marked “For Immediate Release.” Item 2.02 and Heartland’s dated press archive independently confirm that publication date for the actuals. The surviving conference materials leave the earliest qualifying public disclosure unverified.

cases.source_note: The June monthly update covered May revenue per day. It does not set a hard full-quarter bound.
cases.reason: July 26, 2023 is the earliest qualifying disclosure I could verify. Old Dominion reported Q2 consolidated revenue of $1,413,189,000, down 15.2% from $1,667,448,000 and below the $1,584,075,600 cutoff. The April call described a conditional scenario, and the June 5 update covered May. The remaining material gap is CEO Greg Gantt’s June 7 UBS fireside chat. Contemporary reporting establishes that he discussed freight demand, but I could not recover the full remarks, an ODFL presentation, or evidence establishing what was publicly available that day. The dollar value below is the verified July actual. ODFL’s release archive timestamps the Q2 results July 26, 2023 at 7:00 a.m. EDT. Exhibit 99.1 independently dates the announcement July 26. This establishes public availability of the actuals before the August 4 Form 10-Q. The unrecovered June 7 remarks prevent certification of the earliest date.

cases.source_note: Consolidated Q1 revenue in thousands, distinct from drilling, offshore and other segment outlooks.
cases.reason: Oil States publicly established the threshold crossing by April 26, 2024. Its consolidated GAAP revenue for the three months ended March 31, 2024 was $167,262,000 versus $196,199,000 a year earlier, below the $186,389,050 cutoff. The segment realignment transferred operations within Oil States and preserved the consolidated comparison. The earliest date remains unresolved. Two document indexes list a December 1, 2023 investor presentation, but I could not recover its slides or verify its host. I also located the issuer-designated earnings-call replay URLs but could not retrieve the recordings. The April 26 Houston dateline in Exhibit 99.1 and the express publication statement in Item 2.02 establish the public date of the actual. The dollar field records that actual. The missing December slides and unavailable official replays prevent certifying April 26 as the earliest qualifying disclosure.

cases.reason: March 28, 2024 is the earliest explicit, qualifying Q4 sales statement I verified. Reed’s reported $11,693,000 of net sales for the three months ended December 31, 2023, down 22.25% from $15,040,000. The November 10 call transcript resolves the main question about that call: management gave only annual sales guidance, and the operator closed Q&A without taking a question. The earliest date remains unverified because the historical event record is incomplete, including the December 12 shareholder meeting. Item 2.02 expressly records that Reed’s issued the Q4 results release on March 28, 2024 and scheduled its call that day. This verifies public disclosure of actuals on March 28. The remaining event-record gaps prevent certifying it as the first disclosure. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1140215/000149315224011777/form8-k.htm
